Read Today's Paper Sebi’s CAS guidelines likely within a week, says chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey SECTIONS Sebi’s CAS guidelines likely within a week, says chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey By Kumar Gaurav , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 10, 2026, 07:28:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the regulator expects to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within a week. The move follows a review of the Closing Auction Session. Sebi is also working on simpler regulations, easier market access, lower compliance costs and stronger technological resilience. THE ECONOMIC TIMES The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. The Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi ) is likely to issue guidelines on the settlement-price mechanism for derivatives on expiry days within about a week, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Saturday. The regulator is examining feedback on its consultation paper following a review of the Closing Auction Session (CAS). “Following review of the Closing Auction Session, a consultation paper was put out to address concerns in respect of settlement price of derivatives on expiry-day. We are currently examining the comments and hope to issue guidelines in about a week’s time,” Pandey said at the second Capital Market Confluence 2026, organised by the Bombay Stock Exchange Brokers’ Forum in Mumbai. The CAS review is part of Sebi’s broader efforts to deepen India’s cash markets, improve price discovery and enhance market efficiency. Pandey said wider participation, stronger securities borrowing and lending, and efficient hedging and arbitrage could help improve liquidity and the functioning of cash markets. In his address, titled “From Regulation to Global Leadership: Positioning India’s Capital Markets as a Standard-Setter for the Next Decade”, the Sebi chairman outlined four broad priorities for the market regulator: proportionate regulation, deeper cash markets, easier access to Indian markets and greater technological resilience. On the regulatory front, Pandey said Sebi was reviewing the Depositories and Participants Regulations to simplify rules and strengthen fraud prevention. The regulator is also exploring a graded compliance framework for stock brokers based on their scale, client exposure and dependence on technology. Live Events “One size need not fit all,” he said. Sebi is also addressing gaps in the interoperability framework for certain transactions, including tender offers, buybacks and offers for sale (OFS). These transactions currently require parallel clearing arrangements, adding to costs and compliance requirements, Pandey said. The regulator is targeting implementation of the proposed changes by the end of November 2026. The move is expected to improve capital efficiency and lower compliance costs while preserving settlement safety, he said. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-134865747,width-210,height-158,imgsize-184820,resizemode-75/michael-prices-investing-tips-avoid-spreadsheet-traps-ignore-market-consensus-and-be-a-contrarianbr.jpg"> ET Online Michael Price's approach highlights why business fundamentals matter more than short-term market sentiment. Legendary value investor Michael Price believed successful investing requires independent thinking, rigorous research and the discipline to look beyond short-term market movements. His investment philosophy focused on identifying companies trading below their intrinsic value , particularly businesses facing temporary financial difficulties that have the potential to recover. Price developed much of his approach under the guidance of veteran investor Max Heine of Mutual Series Mutual Funds. Over the years, he built a reputation for investing in undervalued companies and identifying opportunities that other market participants may overlook. Look beyond cheap valuations Price believed a low share price or an inexpensive valuation does not automatically make a stock an attractive investment. Investors must establish whether a company's intrinsic value is significantly higher than its current market price. Live Events Traditional valuation measures, including the price-to-book and price-to-cash-flow ratios, can help investors assess whether a stock is undervalued. However, these metrics must be considered alongside the company's financial position, competitive strengths, management quality and prospects for recovery. Price's strategy involved examining businesses experiencing financial difficulties to determine whether their underlying operations remained fundamentally sound. If the problems are temporary and the company can recover, its shares may offer an opportunity to buy at a substantial discount to their underlying worth. He also recommended examining individual business segments separately and studying mergers and acquisitions to understand how potential buyers value companies and their assets. Elevated US bond yields and crude oil prices continue to pressure markets, while inflation data and geopolitical developments could influence the selling trend. ETMarkets.com FII selloff intensifies! Foreign investors sell Indian equities worth Rs 45,000 crore in just 6 sessions. What can reverse the trend? FII selloff has intensified in October, with foreign investors net selling Indian equities worth Rs 45,125 crore in just six sessions in October so far, nearly the same as the total Rs 45,536 crore outflows recorded in the entire month of September. Analysts have listed factors that could change the trend and ease pressure on the market. The Indian stock market snapped a record eight-week-long losing streak last week, ending with gains despite strong upswings and downswings. Yet, FIIs remained bearish and continued selling Indian equities in every session so far in October. The foreign investors have remained net sellers of Indian equities for 11 consecutive sessions since mid-September. What's behind the massive FII outflows? The sharp FII selloff came as bond yields soared to multi-year highs, making the risk-free returns from the debt market more lucrative than equities. The 10-year US Treasury yield recorded its biggest quarterly increase of the 21st century in the three months ended September, Reuters reported. The yield on 10-year US Treasuries climbed above 5.3%, surpassing its 2007 peak and hitting its highest since early 2002. The 30-year yield has touched 5.6%, also not seen since 2002. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that the rapid acceleration in FII outflows in October so far has taken the total FPI equity selling in 2026 to a whopping Rs 3,60,952 crore. “This massive FPI selling is the primary reason why the Indian market is underperforming this year with negative 13.87% Nifty returns so far in 2026,” he said. Live Events Also read | D-St Exit Rush! Sectors that saw sharpest FII selloff in 2nd half of September When can the trend reverse? From the FPI perspective, the rationale behind the massive outflows is the risk-free return from the 10-year US bonds being above 5.2%, according to the analyst. “So long as the US bond yields remain elevated, FPIs will continue to sell. The scenario will change when the valuations become attractive, and the risk-reward ratio turns favourable for investment,” Vijayakumar explained. Shares of Swan Defence and Heavy Industries rose 4.1% to Rs 2,850 on BSE on Monday after the company emerged as the lowest bidder for a Rs 1,897 crore order to build four medium-range product tankers for a proposed joint venture led by state-run Shipping Corporation of India (SCI). The potential contract would strengthen the shipbuilder's order book as India looks to revive domestic shipbuilding after a gap of 25 years in locally built oil tankers. The stock touched an intraday high of Rs 2,874.55, which was also its 52-week high and the upper price band for the day. The company quoted around $48.9 million per vessel when price bids were opened on Friday, October 9, beating state-run Cochin Shipyard Ltd, which quoted around $4 million more per vessel. Swan Defence's tanker opportunity after 25 years The proposed order involves two firm and two optional dual-fuel-ready medium-range product tankers, each capable of carrying 17,000-18,000 tonnes of cargo. The contract, once signed, would mark the first attempt in a quarter of a century to build oil tankers locally. Swan Defence has a technical tie-up with Samsung Heavy Industries, one of South Korea's top three shipbuilders. The company restarted operations in 2024 under new management led by Swan Corp and has since secured multiple vessel-building contracts. Growing order book supports shipbuilding ambitions The shipyard has secured an order from Energy ONE Ltd to build four dual-fuel ammonia bulk carriers in a deal valued at $240-280 million. It has also won a $227 million contract to build six chemical tankers, each with an 18,000-tonne capacity, for European shipowner Rederiet Stenersen AS. Live Events Separately, Swan Defence has signed a contract with Copenhagen-based Svitzer Group to construct four biofuel-powered TRAnsverse tugs worth around Rs 500 crore. The proposed tanker order comes amid the government's push to strengthen domestic shipbuilding, backed by a Rs 69,725 crore package approved by the Cabinet in September 2025. If finalised, the contract would add to Swan Defence's growing pipeline of orders as the industry seeks to expand local vessel manufacturing. The stock has gained 64% in 2026 so far, supported by renewed investor optimism after the company repaid its outstanding debt ahead of schedule and achieved debt-free status. ETMarkets.com PC Jeweller extends its rally as improved balance sheet strength lifts sentiment. Shares of PC Jeweller continued their strong run, jumping another 5% to hit a fresh 52-week high on Monday and extending their rally to 20% over four consecutive sessions. PC Jeweller shares jumped to Rs 15.50 apiece on Monday morning, more than doubling in less than seven months after hitting a 52-week low of Rs 7.47 apiece in March this year. The sharp rally in the share price over the four straight days has added more than Rs 2,500 crore to the company’s market capitalisation, pulling it up to nearly Rs 15,116 crore. Why are PC Jeweller shares rallying? Overall, PC Jeweller shares have jumped around 64% in 2026 so far and 17% in one week. The renewed optimism was driven by the jeweller completing all its repayments ahead of scheduled due dates and achieving ‘debt-free’ status late in September. Also read | PC Jeweller shares rise as firm becomes debt-free The settlement agreement signed in September 2024 was a one-time settlement between PC Jeweller and a 14-bank consortium led by State Bank of India (SBI), aimed at resolving a stressed loan book that stood at nearly Rs 4,100 crore as of March 2024. Live Events The other consortium members included Union Bank, Punjab National Bank (PNB), Axis Bank, IndusInd Bank, Bank of India, IDBI Bank, Karur Vysya Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Indian Overseas Bank, Canara Bank, Indian Bank, Bank of Baroda and IDFC First Bank. The company said the debt-free status will materially strengthen its balance sheet and financial position. Since the announcement in late September, the company's shares have gained around 10% in around three weeks. PC Jeweller share price PC Jeweller shares have delivered multibagger returns in the long term, jumping around 458% in three years and 427% in five years. The stock has overall jumped 64% so far in 2026. The company's shares have gained nearly 19% in one year and 11% in a month. If global conditions remain adverse, defending the rupee will entail increasingly costly policy trade-offs, requiring a broader response spanning exchange-rate flexibility, liquidity and monetary policy, and structural reforms," Arora said. Brent still hovers above $100 a barrel, and US Treasury yields above 5.2% kept the dollar firm. Meanwhile, the RBI's special window will drain the forex stockpile, people aware said. "We reckon that these oil companies could be buying forex of $5.5-6.5 billion a month, depending on their own earnings on exports and proportion where other currencies are used to settle contracts," Bank of Baroda chief economist Madan Sabnavis said. Emkay's Arora estimated their monthly dollar demand higher at $11–12 billion, which could be rerouted from the spot market to the RBI. ETMarkets.com ICICI Pru AMC Q2 Results: The company's mutual fund quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) rose 14.4% YoY to Rs 11.61 lakh crore ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company on Monday reported a 6.1% year-on-year (YoY) rise in profit after tax (PAT) to Rs 889 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 838 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year. The company’s board also declared an interim dividend of Rs 30 per equity share and fixed October 21, 2026, as the record date for determining eligible shareholders. Revenue from operations rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 1,674 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 1,439 crore in Q2 FY26. Total expenses increased 17.9% to Rs 493 crore during the quarter, from Rs 418 crore a year earlier. For the six months ended September 30, 2026, the company reported a 14.3% YoY increase in PAT to Rs 1,854 crore, compared with Rs 1,622 crore in the corresponding period of the previous financial year. ICICI Prudentia AMC's mutual fund quarterly average assets under management (QAAUM) rose 14.4% YoY to Rs 11.61 lakh crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, from Rs 10.15 lakh crore a year earlier. Its market share stood at 13.3%. The segment had a market share of 13.3%. Assets in equity and equity-oriented schemes rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 6.59 lakh crore, from Rs 5.67 lakh crore, with a market share of 13.7%. Equity-oriented hybrid schemes recorded a 19.7% increase in QAAUM to Rs 2.29 lakh crore, compared with Rs 1.91 lakh crore a year earlier. The segment’s market share stood at 26.4%. In its alternatives business, QAAUM stood at Rs 80,965 crore as of September 30, 2026. Separately, NCLAT has stayed the NCLT order admitting insolvency proceedings against the company over an alleged Rs 2.79 crore operational debt, pending further orders. ETMarkets.com No contracts for new expiry months in Polycab India will be issued after the expiry of existing contract months. The National Stock Exchange (NSE) will exclude Polycab India from the equity derivatives segment with effect from December 30, 2026, according to an exchange's latest circular. The NSE circular stated that no contracts for new expiry months in Polycab India will be issued after the expiry of existing contract months. However, existing unexpired contracts for October, November and December 2026 will continue to be available for trading until their respective expiry dates. New strikes will also be introduced in these existing contract months. No contracts in Polycab India will be available for trading in the equity derivatives segment from December 30, 2026, the exchange said. ALSO READ: Market Trading Guide: Astra Microwave, Manappuram among 5 stock recommendations for Tuesday Separately, Polycab India informed the exchanges that NCLAT had stayed and kept in abeyance the October 7 order passed by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Ahmedabad Bench, admitting the corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) against the company in a case filed by Asier Metals Private Limited. Live Events The proceedings relate to an alleged operational debt of Rs 2.79 crore under Section 9 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. According to the NCLAT order, counsel for Polycab submitted that a pre-existing dispute existed between the parties concerning payments made and credit notes to be issued by the operational creditor. The company's counsel also submitted that Polycab was willing to deposit the entire amount stated in Part IV of the insolvency application, without prejudice to its rights and contentions. The tribunal directed that the amount be deposited through a fixed deposit receipt (FDR) in the name of the Registrar, NCLAT, New Delhi, within a week. It stayed the NCLT's October 7 order and kept it in abeyance until further orders. Polycab India shares settled 1.82% higher at Rs 8,405 apiece on the NSE on Monday, compared with the previous close of Rs 8,255. During the session, the stock traded between Rs 8,291 and Rs 8,469. The stock has gained nearly 10% so far in 2026, while the Nifty 50 has declined nearly 14% over the same period, according to the data provided. The Nifty 50 advanced 358 points, or 1.60%, to settle at 22,722, while the BSE Sensex climbed 1,109 points, or 1.54%, to close at 73,034. Read Today's Paper Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% SECTIONS Tata Elxsi Q2 Results: Profit rises 10% YoY to Rs 170 crore; revenue grows 15% By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 13, 2026, 06:15:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Tata Elxsi reported a 10% year-on-year rise in net profit to Rs 170 crore in Q2, while revenue from operations grew 15% to Rs 1,056 crore. Higher employee and operating expenses, along with lower other income, weighed on margins. Net profit for the first half of FY27 rose 14%. ETMarkets.com Tata Elxsi on Tuesday reported a 10% year-on-year (YoY) rise in net profit for the September quarter, helped by double-digit growth in revenue even as higher employee and operating costs kept profit growth below the top-line expansion. The company’s net profit for the quarter ended September stood at Rs 170 crore, compared with Rs 155 crore in the same period last year. Revenue from operations rose 15% YoY to Rs 1,056 crore from Rs 918 crore a year earlier. Total income from operations, including other income, increased 13% to Rs 1,090 crore, compared with Rs 967 crore a year earlier. Other income fell to Rs 35 crore from Rs 49 crore, partly weighing on the overall profit growth. Profit before tax rose 11% to Rs 239 crore from Rs 215 crore in the year-ago quarter. Total tax expense increased to Rs 69 crore from Rs 60 crore. There was no exceptional item in the quarter. The company’s total expenses grew 13% YoY to Rs 851 crore from Rs 752 crore. Employee benefit expenses, the largest cost item for the company, rose 15% to Rs 620 crore from Rs 539 crore. Other expenses also increased 15% to Rs 131 crore from Rs 114 crore. Cost of materials consumed rose marginally to Rs 73 crore from Rs 72 crore. Depreciation and amortisation expense stood at Rs 24 crore, compared with Rs 23 crore a year earlier. Finance costs declined to Rs 3.57 crore from Rs 4 crore. Live Events Also read: Reliance Jio said to see over $20 billion bids as investors line up for India's biggest IPO The company’s profit before tax margin on revenue from operations stood at 22.7%, compared with 23.4% a year earlier. Net profit margin also moderated to 16.1% from 16.9%, reflecting the impact of higher costs and lower other income. Net profit for the six-month period increased 14% to Rs 341 crore, compared with Rs 299 crore in the same period last year. Profit before tax for the April-September period rose 15% to Rs 472 crore from Rs 411 crore. Total income from operations stood at Rs 2,153 crore, up 13% from Rs 1,897 crore a year earlier. After her recent comments sparked hopes for a tax rejig among investors, analysts noted that such easing would result in FIIs finally making their much-awaited comeback, which in turn would be favourable for the wounded bulls on Dalal Street. Following the 2024 General Elections, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in July announced an overhaul in the way India taxes profits made from the equity stock market. The tax on short-term capital gains (STCG), which essentially are profits booked within one year of purchase, was raised from 15% to 20%, while long-term capital gains tax on equities was increased from 10% to 12.5%. FII outflows intensified since 2024 Analysts had warned that the changes would spook FIIs out of Dalal Street, and the warning unfortunately came true. Foreign investors net sold Indian equities worth Rs 2,774 crore from July till the end of 2024. Fuelled by multiple headwinds including Trump’s tariff flip-flops, the Middle East war, a weakening rupee and soaring bond yields, the FII sell-off intensified over the years. FII outflows jumped to Rs 1.66 lakh crore in 2025 and Rs 3.06 lakh crore in 2026 so far. Such heavy selling by foreign investors has added to the headwinds pressuring Indian equities following the sharp bull run of 2024.

The anchor book saw strong participation from domestic mutual funds, insurance companies and global institutional investors. Out of the total anchor allocation, 21,05,565 shares, or 57.72% of the anchor portion, were allotted to 12 domestic mutual funds through 25 schemes. Jio IPO: Reservation and record date details The record date for determining eligible Reliance Industries shareholders has been fixed as October 14, 2026, the same day Jio Platforms filed its red herring prospectus. Reliance Jio sets aside Rs 2,500 crore shares in IPO reservation Because Indian equities follow a T+1 settlement cycle, investors generally need to buy shares at least one trading day before the record date for the shares to be credited to their demat account on time. NSE says trades in rolling settlement are settled on a T+1 basis, meaning settlement happens on the next working day after the trade. Live Events In simple terms, investors who wanted to qualify for the Jio shareholder quota needed to have bought RIL shares by October 13. Buying RIL shares on October 14 or later will not make an investor eligible for the quota because those shares would normally settle after the eligibility date. What Jio IPO means for RIL shareholders For RIL shareholders, this quota gives a separate route to apply for shares in Jio Platforms. Until now, public investors could get exposure to Jio mainly through Reliance Industries shares. By Nikhil Agarwal , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 15, 2026, 09:53:00 AM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis The Indian stock market is witnessing a notable transformation as large-cap stocks are losing ground amidst changing capital flows and investor sentiment. Mid- and small-cap companies are surging ahead, capturing more market capitalization as domestic institutional investors pivot towards these segments. As large-caps endure foreign selling pressures, the contrast in performance underscores a shift in market dynamics. Future outcomes will hinge on whether earnings growth aligns with current valuations. " src="https://img.etimg.com/thumb/msid-134957295,width-210,height-158,imgsize-1892078,resizemode-75/largecaps-are-shrinking-smallcaps-are-getting-bigger-what-is-changing-in-indias-stock-marketbr.jpg"> ETMarkets.com India’s stock market hierarchy is undergoing a quiet but significant shift. Largecaps , long seen as the core of institutional portfolios, are losing their share of the market even as mid- and smallcap companies expand their footprint. The combined market capitalisation share of mid- and smallcaps reached a record 43.7% in September, while the share of the top 100 companies fell to a low of 56.3%, according to data from Motilal Oswal Financial Services . The shift has been accompanied by a sharp performance gap. In the first half of FY27, the Nifty50 rose just 1.3%, while the Nifty Smallcap 250 gained 24.6%, according to Prateek Nigudkar, senior fund manager at Shriram AMC . “The defining feature of the quarter was the sharp divergence between largecaps and the broader market,” Nigudkar said. The divergence, however, is not necessarily a straightforward verdict on fundamentals. It has been shaped significantly by the direction of capital flows. Foreign investors, who typically own a larger share of India’s biggest companies, have been selling largecaps as global bond yields rose, the rupee weakened and oil prices climbed. Domestic institutions, supported by steady systematic investment plan inflows, have directed more money towards mid- and smallcap stocks. “Largecaps, owned heavily by foreign investors, have borne the brunt of global risk-off selling, while smaller companies, owned mostly by domestic investors, have been cushioned by steady SIP inflows,” Nigudkar said. Live Events That flow-driven divergence has created a new market paradox where smaller companies now account for a record share of India’s market, but largecaps are beginning to look more attractive on valuations. Read Today's Paper Sebi revises CAS rules, changes derivatives expiry settlement methodology SECTIONS Sebi revises CAS rules, changes derivatives expiry settlement methodology By Akash Podishetti , ETMarkets.com Last Updated: Oct 15, 2026, 09:45:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Sebi has announced changes to the closing auction session for the equity cash market, which will begin in December 2026. The revised session will run from 3.30 pm to 3.40 pm, with specific phases for order entry. Moreover, the methodology for calculating settlement prices for derivatives contracts has been updated. Unexecuted orders will transition under new rules while maintaining time priority differences. Agencies Sebi has revised the rules and norms related to closing auction session and derivatives expiry settlement methodology. Capital markets regulator Sebi has revised the framework for the closing auction session in the equity cash market , including changes to trading timings , the treatment of unexecuted orders and the calculation of settlement prices for derivatives contracts. Under the revised framework, the closing auction session (CAS) will run from 3.30 pm to 3.40 pm on all trading days. The changes will take effect from December 7, 2026, except for modifications governing the transition of unexecuted limit and iceberg orders from the continuous trading session, which will come into force on February 8, 2027. Sebi introduced the closing auction session to facilitate transparent and efficient price discovery for closing prices of securities. Following its implementation, the regulator reviewed aspects of the framework and sought public comments through a consultation paper issued on September 12. The revised schedule divides the 10-minute auction into three phases. The first minute, starting at 3.30 pm, will be used to calculate the reference price and transition orders from the continuous trading session. Order entry for both limit and market orders will be permitted from 3.31 pm to 3.36 pm, followed by a four-minute period during which only limit orders can be entered. Market orders cannot be modified or cancelled during this final phase. The order-entry window will close randomly between 3.38 pm and 3.40 pm. Trading in index derivatives will continue until 3.45 pm on regular trading days, but contracts expiring that day will stop trading at 3.30 pm. Stock derivatives will continue trading until 3.45 pm, including on expiry days. The post-close session in the cash market will run from 3.50 pm to 4 pm, with trades executed at the closing price of the securities. The settlement price of expiring index derivatives will be based on the value of the underlying index calculated using the volume-weighted average prices (VWAP) of its constituent securities during the final 30 minutes of the continuous trading session in the equity cash market. For expiring stock derivatives, clearing corporations will determine settlement prices using the VWAP of the underlying stock during the final 30 minutes of the cash market session across all stock exchanges.
